resolver.kicker: Entry 01 · Agentic AI · Sopra Steria, curricular internship (MSc AI)
resolver.title: An incident resolver that has to show its work
resolver.standfirst: The brief is not a chatbot. It is an agent that takes an L1/L2 support incident, classifies it, gathers evidence, proposes a diagnosis, acts only inside a safety policy, asks a person before anything sensitive, and verifies the result before calling the incident closed.
resolver.problem: Most L1/L2 tickets are repetitive: a locked account, a VPN that won't stay connected, a missing folder permission. But an LLM that answers a ticket is not one that resolves it safely. The engineering problem is control: deciding when the agent may act, recording why it acted, and knowing when to hand over.
resolver.role: I am building the prototype as my master's internship challenge, working on the backend, the incident routing, its evaluation and the workflow around them. It runs only against simulated scenarios: no real credentials, users or corporate systems.

status.t: FastAPI backend with OIDC authentication and a mock mode for development.
LLM incident router: classification, fallback to a human and a background judge, with an offline evaluation harness.
Web client (Vue 3, TypeScript): chat, approvals and ticket flow, currently on mocked data.
Agent graph, hybrid retrieval over runbooks (embeddings + BM25) and diagnostic tools.
Sandboxed execution, policy gates and verification of the outcome.

resolver.scope: Stack in the challenge scope: Python, FastAPI, LangGraph, PostgreSQL + pgvector, Redis, Pydantic, Docker Compose, automated evaluation. Listed as scope, not as finished work.
resolver.confidential: Private repository. Described at the level of the public challenge; no code, data, prompts or internal documents are published here.
resolver.figTitle: Incident resolution as a state machine
resolver.figCaption: Conceptual flow of the target system; each stage carries its current status. The trace is a synthetic incident written for this page.

trace.m: “VPN connects, then drops after a few seconds.”
network / vpn · confidence high → automated path
hypothesis: expired client certificate · evidence: handshake log

principles.t: Policies decide what the agent may do alone. Anything sensitive waits for a person, and low confidence routes to a human instead of to a guess.
Every transition records its input, evidence and decision, so an intervention can be audited after the fact.
A resolution only counts once it is verified. The measure is incidents correctly closed or correctly escalated, not fluent answers.

f1.kicker: Entry 02 · Machine learning · Personal project · MIT licence
f1.title: Predicting a championship from forty-five labels
f1.standfirst: After every Grand Prix, the model estimates each driver's probability of winning that season's World Championship. The interesting part is not the prediction. It is refusing to fool yourself on a problem with one positive label per season.
f1.problem: The modelling set has 21,072 driver-round rows but only about 45 independent outcomes: one champion per season since 1981. A random split leaks a season's ending into its own beginning, and a pooled ROC AUC mostly measures how obvious the last rounds are.
approach: Walk-forward validation on whole seasons: 30 expanding-window folds, never a random split.
Six model families compared on group log-loss; the winner picked by a one-standard-error rule that prefers the simpler model.
Platt calibration on held-out seasons, then each round's probabilities normalised to sum to 1, with mathematically eliminated drivers set to 0.
Every metric stratified by season phase and printed next to the “leader wins” baseline.
Predictions flagged in-sample or out-of-sample, so replaying history cannot pass for accuracy.
f1.foldsCaption: Each row is one fold: seasons that train the base model, three that fit the calibrator, one held-out test season. Derived from conf/models.yaml. 2026 is in progress and is only ever predicted.
f1.zooCaption: Mean group log-loss over 30 folds, lower is better. The dashed line sits one standard error above the best; only logistic regression falls inside it.
f1.sheetCaption: Out-of-fold results of the active model by season phase, beside the baseline.
f1.ablation: Ablation: refitting on only the top 5 features by permutation importance roughly doubles the loss, from 0.615 to 1.232.
engineering: {tests} test functions: unit tests plus integration tests against a real database, a real fitted model and a real MLflow store.
Ruff, Black and mypy --strict in CI, which then builds the Docker images and brings the full stack up behind health checks.
A nightly workflow re-ingests data, rebuilds the dataset and retrains.
Behaviour pinned in OpenSpec capability specs; two self-audits are recorded in the repository alongside their fixes.
limits: n ≈ 45. A few genuinely open seasons account for a large share of the loss.
No hyperparameter search. LightGBM sits 0.001 outside the threshold, so the ranking needs re-checking after each retrain.
The deployed model is refit on almost every season; only the walk-forward numbers are honest evidence.

exte.title: The internal platform a team works in every day
exte.standfirst: exte.market is EXTE's internal application, where the markets team does its day-to-day work: campaign dashboards, planning, deals and opportunities, and marketplace configuration, all organised by workspace. I build and maintain the services behind it and a good part of the interface.

themes.t: The planner: a map view and a planning view that build campaigns from formats and business formulas, with geospatial proximity (points of interest × screen radius). Planning that took days of manual coordination now takes minutes.
Per-workspace campaign metrics stored in Elasticsearch, aggregated and served to Vue.js dashboards.
The deals and opportunities flow of each workspace, and the configuration of the marketplaces it is connected to, kept in sync with three external DOOH platforms over their REST APIs.
A vector-tile map layer: MBTiles served by a Martin tile server and rendered with MapLibre / Mapbox.
Reusable Vue.js components contributed to the company's design system and shared across products.
Secure REST APIs (OAuth2, JWT) on Symfony / Yii2, MariaDB and Docker; GitLab CI/CD with automated tests and automated deployments.
Maintaining and evolving the company's legacy systems, and working on the project that centralises them.

exte.stack: PHP · Symfony · Yii2 · Python · FastAPI · Node.js · Vue.js · TypeScript · MariaDB · Elasticsearch · Docker · GitLab CI/CD · Linux · MapLibre · MBTiles

workshop.title: Smaller tools, each built for a real use

expenses.text: Upload a bank statement (CaixaBank format or generic CSV/XLSX) and get categorised spending, monthly balance, anomalies and recommendations. A FastAPI backend with vectorised pandas analytics; a Streamlit client that talks to it only over HTTP; an optional plain-language summary from a local Ollama model, off by default so no data has to leave the machine.

cutting.text: A tool built for MAFAC, an aluminium carpentry workshop. It works out how many stock bars a cutting list needs using first-fit decreasing, and warns about off-cuts too short to survive the saw. Login-protected with hashed credentials and JWT.
cutting.figCaption: The repository's algorithm, re-run on an illustrative cutting list with stock length 650. Shaded: off-cut.

chess.text: A complete chess game in Java, written with a classmate for a software-quality course: legal-move validation for every piece, and a test suite built alongside the code with JUnit 5 and Mockito.

trajectory.title: From CRUD apps to AI systems
trajectory.intro: I started where most people do: CRUD apps, forms and APIs. At EXTE that grew into microservices, integrations with external platforms, automation and geospatial systems in production. The master's and the internship are the next step on the same line: systems where the model is one component and everything around it (data, evaluation, control) has to be engineered.

timeline.n: Information Technology specialisation; software quality with tests (entry 06).
Intern from September 2024, on the team since February 2025. From CRUDs to microservices, integrations and geospatial (entry 03).
Campaign planning with an interactive map, geographic filters and points of interest. Graded 9.9/10.
A local LLM (Ollama) inside a FastAPI app (entry 04).
With the Generative AI PSU. ML, NLP, computer vision, MLOps.
ML with temporal validation, MLflow and CI (entry 02).

trajectory.looking: Software Engineer or AI Systems Engineer roles, and AI, ML or MLOps engineering: teams where production-grade backend standards meet applied AI, where I can take a system from the model to the product, and keep learning from people further along.
